theory.intro: **Quadrantal angles** have their terminal arm along a coordinate axis: $0^{\circ}, 90^{\circ}, 180^{\circ}, 270^{\circ}, 360^{\circ}$, and other multiples of $90^{\circ}$. On the unit circle ($r=1$), their points $P(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ are $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, $(-1,0)$, and $(0,-1)$.
facts: $\tan\theta$ is undefined at odd multiples of $90^{\circ}$ ($90^{\circ}, 270^{\circ}, 450^{\circ}, -90^{\circ}$) because $x=0$ ($\cos\theta=0$).
For all integer multiples of $180^{\circ}$ ($0^{\circ}, 180^{\circ}, 360^{\circ}, -180^{\circ}$), $\sin\theta=0$ and $\tan\theta=0$.

foundation.question_text: Using the unit circle point $P(0,1)$ at $\theta=90^{\circ}$, state the exact values of $\cos 90^{\circ}$ and $\sin 90^{\circ}$.
Using the unit circle point $P(-1,0)$ at $\theta=180^{\circ}$, state the exact values of $\cos 180^{\circ}$ and $\sin 180^{\circ}$.
Explain using coordinates on the unit circle why $\tan 90^{\circ}$ is undefined.
foundation.solution_text:
At $\theta=90^{\circ}$, $P(x,y)=(0,1)$, so $x=0$ and $y=1$.
$\tan 90^{\circ}=\dfrac{y}{x}=\dfrac{1}{0}$
Division by zero is undefined, so $\tan 90^{\circ}$ is undefined.

foundation.question_text: State the exact values of $\cos 270^{\circ}$ and $\sin 270^{\circ}$.
foundation.solution_text:
At $\theta=270^{\circ}$, the point on the unit circle is $(0,-1)$.
$\cos 270^{\circ}=0$
$\sin 270^{\circ}=-1$

foundation.question_text:
State whether $\tan 180^{\circ}$ and $\tan 270^{\circ}$ are defined.
Give their values or write 'undefined'.
foundation.solution_text:
At $180^{\circ}$, $P=(-1,0)$, so $\tan 180^{\circ}=\dfrac{0}{-1}=0$ (defined).
At $270^{\circ}$, $P=(0,-1)$, so $\tan 270^{\circ}=\dfrac{-1}{0}$ is undefined.

foundation.question_text: Find all angles $\theta$ in the domain $0^{\circ}\le\theta<360^{\circ}$ for which $\sin\theta=0$.
foundation.solution_text:
$\sin\theta$ is the $y$-coordinate on the unit circle.
$y=0$ occurs at $(1,0)$ and $(-1,0)$.
$\theta=0^{\circ}\text{ and }180^{\circ}$

development.question_text: Evaluate $\cos(-90^{\circ})$ and $\sin(-90^{\circ})$ using coordinates on the unit circle.
development.solution_text:
$-90^{\circ}$ corresponds to $(0,-1)$ on the unit circle (same as $270^{\circ}$).
$\cos(-90^{\circ})=0$
$\sin(-90^{\circ})=-1$

$450^{\circ}-360^{\circ}=90^{\circ}$, which corresponds to $(0,1)$ on the unit circle.
$\sin 450^{\circ}=1$
$\cos 450^{\circ}=0$

development.question_text: List all angles $\theta$ in the domain $0^{\circ}\le\theta\le 360^{\circ}$ where $\tan\theta$ is undefined, and state why.
development.solution_text:
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ is undefined wherever $\cos\theta=0$.
On $0^{\circ}\le\theta\le 360^{\circ}$, $\cos\theta=0$ at $\theta=90^{\circ}$ and $\theta=270^{\circ}$.
Therefore $\tan\theta$ is undefined at $\theta=90^{\circ}\text{ and }270^{\circ}$.

$\cos\theta=-1$ corresponds to the point $(-1,0)$ on the unit circle.
$\theta=180^{\circ}$

$\sin\theta=-1$ corresponds to the point $(0,-1)$ on the unit circle.
$\theta=270^{\circ}$

development.question_text:
The point $P(0,-6)$ lies on the terminal arm of angle $\theta$ on a circle centred at the origin.
Find $\theta$ in $0^{\circ}\le\theta<360^{\circ}$ and state $\cos\theta$, $\sin\theta$, and $\tan\theta$.
development.solution_text:
$P(0,-6)$ lies on the negative $y$-axis, so $\theta=270^{\circ}$ and $r=6$.
$\cos 270^{\circ}=\dfrac{0}{6}=0$
$\sin 270^{\circ}=\dfrac{-6}{6}=-1$
$\tan 270^{\circ}=\dfrac{-6}{0}\text{ is undefined}$

mastery.question_text: Evaluate the exact value of the expression $\dfrac{5\sin 90^{\circ} + 2\cos 180^{\circ}}{\cos 360^{\circ} - \sin 270^{\circ}}$.

A circle centred at the origin passes through the point $(-7,0)$ at angle $\theta$ with $0^{\circ}\le\theta<360^{\circ}$.
Find $\theta$ and evaluate $4\sin\theta - 3\cos\theta + \tan\theta$.
Find all values of $\theta$ in $0^{\circ}\le\theta\le 360^{\circ}$ that satisfy $\sin^2\theta + \cos\theta = 1$ using boundary angles.
